observed_mechanics: 22 instructions, 0x005a2ed0..0x005a2f1c inclusive, 79 bytes, one terminator: RET 0x4 at 0x005a2f1c
PUSH ESI / MOV ESI,ECX -- the receiver is aliased into ESI at 0x005a2ed1 and every receiver access goes through that alias
ECX is REWRITTEN at 0x005a2ee7 with the word loaded from receiver+0x10, and nothing between there and the CALL at 0x005a2ef3 rewrites it again, so the callee receives the POINTEE
three unconditional 32-bit stores of three distinct .rdata immediates at +0x00 (0x013f69c8), +0x04 (0x013f69b8) and +0x08 (0x013f69b4), in ASCENDING displacement, at 0x005a2ed3/0x005a2ed9/0x005a2ee0
one 32-bit READ at receiver+0x10 (0x005a2ee7) -- the only receiver word this body reads
the word at +0x10 is a POINTER, and the body dereferences it exactly once before treating what it reads as a table: MOV EAX,[ECX] at 0x005a2eee has no displacement, so it is the pointee's own +0x00
TEST ECX,ECX at 0x005a2eea with JZ rel8 at 0x005a2eec -- the guard is on the loaded word being zero, and it skips the call and nothing else
the dispatch is a TWO-LEVEL table load: MOV EDX,[EAX+0x4] at 0x005a2ef0 is slot displacement 0x04, i.e. dword index 1, and CALL EDX at 0x005a2ef3 passes ECX (the pointee) with no stack word pushed

TEST BYTE PTR [ESP+0x8],0x1 at 0x005a2ef5 -- the body's only stack read, a BYTE, and the 0x8 is not an ordinary frame offset: one word is outstanding (the prologue's saved ESI), so entry_ESP-4+0x8 == entry_ESP+0x4, the first ordinary stack argument and the four bytes RET 0x4 pops
the flag is read AFTER the guarded call and BEFORE the second triple, which is observable: an observer inside the call can overwrite the flag byte and the body then acts on the modified value

three more unconditional 32-bit stores at +0x08 (0x013ef094), +0x04 (0x013eb394) and +0x00 (0x013eb938), in DESCENDING displacement, at 0x005a2efa/0x005a2f01/0x005a2f08 -- the reverse of the first triple's order, and three addresses disjoint from the first triple's three

the three second-triple stores sit between the TEST at 0x005a2ef5 and the JZ at 0x005a2f0e, so they happen on the deleting path and the non-deleting path alike; the MOVs write no flags, so the JZ consumes exactly the flags the TEST set
JZ rel8 at 0x005a2f0e is TAKEN when bit 0 of the flag byte is CLEAR, so the deallocation runs when bit 0 is SET -- the mask is 0x1, not 'non-zero'
PUSH ESI / CALL 0x00f47380 / ADD ESP,0x4 at 0x005a2f10/0x005a2f11/0x005a2f16 -- one direct call, the receiver as the single pushed word, caller-cleaned

0x00f47380's own body is seven instructions ending in a BARE C3 with no immediate (MOV EAX,[ESP+0x4] / TEST EAX,EAX / JZ / MOV EAX,[0x016c8b44] / PUSH EAX / CALL 0x009276c0 / RET), which is what makes the cdecl reading a fact rather than a habit: it pops nothing but the return address, so the ADD at 0x005a2f16 is the caller dropping the word, and its first instruction with no push outstanding fixes the argument and its order

MOV EAX,ESI at 0x005a2f19 is the last write to EAX before the sole RET, it is unconditional, and ESI has not been rewritten since 0x005a2ed1 -- so the return value is the RECEIVER on both paths and is not a re-read of the receiver's memory

POP ESI at 0x005a2f1b restores the prologue's push, so the frame is balanced before RET 0x4 consumes the return address and the one argument word
no instruction in the body is a register-to-memory or memory-operand transfer other than the six immediate stores; the only absolute operands are the six .rdata immediates and the direct call target

observed_original_abi.return_note: HONEST DISCLOSURE, because this field is a worker claim and not a machine token. The machine ABI envelope for this VA records return_semantics "unclassified_in_EAX" with return {register EAX, register_class "aggregate_unknown", type null, void_possible false} -- machine-vocabulary phrases that name no C++ type. Independently of that envelope the complete listing fixes the value: MOV EAX,ESI at 0x005a2f19 is the last write to EAX before the body's sole RET at 0x005a2f1c, it is unconditional on both paths, and ESI has held the receiver since 0x005a2ed1, so the returned value is the receiver pointer and the deallocation callee's return is discarded. Ghidra's own decompilation of this body agrees (`return param_1`). The return_type published here is therefore derived FROM THE LISTING at those two addresses, and its SPELLING is this package's own type name, not a name recovered from the image -- SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI. Per the worker contract section 7.1, option (a) was taken: the source declares the return type that is true of the listing, the machine envelope's own token is recorded verbatim alongside it, and the residual disagreement is listed in unresolved_questions. No typedef was invented after the phrase 'unclassified_in_EAX' to win the validator's string comparison, and void was NOT declared because the bytes genuinely produce a value.

mechanics.receiver_displacement: The body reaches exactly four receiver displacements -- 0x00, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10 -- and all four are reached through the ESI alias rather than through ECX's own operands. The machine-derived record enumerates exactly [0, 4, 8, 16] with bounds_only true, so here the record and the listing AGREE and the disagreement wave-1 packages had to argue about does not arise. No member is named for any displacement; the source reaches the receiver through displacement-named accessors, and the pointee's own +0x00 is the one member declared anywhere in the package, because it is witnessed by the listing at a displacement of the pointee rather than of the receiver
mechanics.pointer_levels: Two levels, and that is the single highest-risk item in the body. receiver+0x10 is a pointer; the pointee's +0x00 is a table pointer; the table's +0x04 is the callee. Reading the +0x10 word as a dispatch word, passing receiver+0x10 instead of the pointee to the callee, and calling the table's slot 0 instead of its slot 1 are three distinct wrong machines, and the package's own test fixture was written wrong in the first two forms before it caught them
mechanics.store_ordering: The two triples are stored in OPPOSITE displacement orders -- first triple ascending (+0x00, +0x04, +0x08), second triple descending (+0x08, +0x04, +0x00) -- and the final memory state is identical whichever order a body uses, so only an in-body log can separate the two readings. Both orderings are observable from inside the two callees as well: at the dispatch the three words must already hold the FIRST triple and none of the second, and at the deallocation they must already hold the second triple's three
mechanics.globals: None beyond the six .rdata immediates, which are STORED and never read. The xref export carries data_reference_count 0 for this VA, so the validator's GLOBALS dimension has no second machine side to corroborate a data address's mode against and will WARN for any body that stores one. That is a property of the evidence, not a defect in the source, and the stores are declared rather than omitted -- omitting them would falsify the body

validation.model_test: plain int main() with explicit checks, no framework and no external dependency: 100 checks over 16 cases, 0 failures. Both callees are observers -- deallocate_00f47380 is defined in the test and the dispatch slot is reached only through a pointer the test installs in a table of its own, exactly as `ff d2` does. Four distinct dispatch observers sit in slots 0, 1, 2 and 3 of that table so the slot displacement is MEASURED, and the observers can overwrite the deleting-flag byte and the receiver's first word so the flag's read point and the return value's provenance are observable rather than assumed. The receiver image carries a 0x20-byte guard band on each side and the test byte-diffs the whole buffer, so 'no byte outside the six store displacements changed' is asserted rather than assumed. Cases: A the ordered store log (count, displacements, values, and the descending order of the second triple, which the final memory state cannot show); B the final state plus the guarded byte diff; C the null guard; D the slot displacement; E two-level dereference against a decoy table at the address receiver+0x10; F the callee's receiver is the pointee and neither of the two other candidates; G the flag is bit 0 and not 'non-zero', driven with 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x80 and 0xff; H the deallocation's argument; I all six stores complete before the deallocation; J the flag is read after the dispatch, proved by overwriting the flag byte from inside the call; K the returned pointer is the receiver and not a re-read of it; L the deallocation callee's return is discarded; M the two guards are independent, driven over all four combinations; N the six immediates and their pairwise distinctness; O the displacement constants and the frame arithmetic; P the first triple is installed and the second is not, at the instant of the dispatch.
